entities.text:
High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Shri Harjas Singh Chhabra - Advocate for the applic
 Shri C.M.Tiwari- G.A. for the respondent/State.
ORDER This first application under Section 482 of The Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita has been filed on behalf of the applicant for grant of anticipatory bail.

2. Applicant apprehending his arrest in connection with Crime No. 158/2025 of Police Station-Omti,
District-Jabalpur (MP) for commission of the offences punishable under Sections 409, 419, 420,
467, 468, 471, 120B of IPC and Section 316(5), 319(2), 318(4), 338, 336(3), 340(2) and 61 of BNS has knocked the portal of this Court for grant of anticipatory bail.
3.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that at the relevant time, applicant was posted as bill preparator in the office.
He used to prepare the salary bill etc. and after preparing the same, he used to send the same to Sandeep Sharma.
At the time of creation of ID, Sandeep Saharma used to change the amount as well as account number.
Every thing has been done by NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:37257 2 MCRC-15198-2025 the co-accused Sandeep Sharma at the stage of creation of ID.
Sandeep Sharma has admitted that he is behind all this.

In departmental inquiry,
whole allegations have been levelled against Sandeep Sharma.
It is also urged that only an amount Rs. 2,53,000/-has been credited into amount of applicant as DA.
It is urged that applicant's brother and wife are not accused in the instant case.

It is also urged that case of present case is identical to Anoop Kumar Bouriya vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85693636/
1

entities.text: Anoop Kumar Bouriya vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: co- accused persons Swati Sharma, Poonam, Sweta etc. who have been released on bail by Coordinate bench of this court vide order dated 26.05.2025 passed in M.Cr.C. No. 23444/2025.
Applicant is ready to abide by all the conditions whatsoever imposed by this Court.
On these grounds, learned counsel for the applicant prays for grant of anticipatory bail.

4. Per-contra, learned counsel for the respondent-State, while opposing the anticipatory bail application, submits that at relevant point of time, applicant was posted as creator of salary bill and other voucher etc.
Further, it is also urged that an amount of Rs. 2,63,948/- has been credited into the account of applicant.
Further, Rs. 58,130/- has been credited into the account of applicant's brother Abhay and Rs. 25,81,904/- has been credited into the account of applicant's wife Jaya.
Therefore, he has prayed for dismissal of the anticipatory bail application.

5. Having regard to the factual matrix of the case as well as nature of evidence available on record pertaining to applicant's involvement in the offence, without expressing any opinion on the merit of the case, I am of the view that it is a case in which applicant may be released on bail.

Consequently,
anticipatory bail application filed on behalf of applicant stands NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:37257 3 MCRC-15198-2025 allowed.

6. It is directed that in the event of his arrest, applicant be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond of Rs.15,000/- (Rupees Fifteen Thousand Only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the Arresting Officer.

It is also directed that the applicant shall abide by the conditions as enumerated under Section 482(2) of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita,
2023.

It is made clear that applicant shall appear before the Investigating Officer as & when he is so directed and cooperate with the investigation and he shall also appear before the Trial Court failing which his bail shall automatically stand cancelled without further reference to the Court.
7. C.C. as per rules.
(ACHAL KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE L.R.
